teach_en: The stroke າ is part of three different vowels. Look at what is written before and above the consonant to tell them apart. || ◌າ | aa | the a in 'father' || ເ◌ົາ | ao | the ow in 'now' || ◌ຳ | am | the o in 'Tom' (American), short
notes: Recap card, not a pronunciation rule (owner 2026-11-09, LESSON_PLAN decision 18): the same stroke appears in V03, V35 and V36, which looks like a contradiction unless it is pointed out. Format: prose, then rows separated by ' || ', each row 'Lao | sounds like | cue' (the app shows them as a table). Sounds are the respellings of V03, V35, V36 (vowels are the same in both transliteration styles); cues repeat the units' teach texts. Wording by agent. R01 is reserved for dead syllables. A4 2026-11-13: hint revised, owner + formant check.

teach_en: A syllable like ສະ stops sharply, with a tiny catch in the throat, as in the break in 'uh-oh'.
notes: Rule R01 (dead syllables), first card (owner decision 25: one brief line, no rule to memorise; decision 11: no tone or length wording). Covers only the short-open case met so far (V01 ◌ະ); syllables ending in k, t, p are a later card. 'Catch in the throat' restates the glottal stop in the V01 IPA aʔ and the C26 letters.csv wording. Wording by agent and curriculum review.

teach_en: Lao vowels can sit before, above, below or after the consonant. Some come in several parts around it, and all the parts make one vowel. However a vowel is written, you say the consonant first and the vowel second. The next vowel, ເ◌ົາ, starts on the page before its consonant: read past it to the consonant, then say the vowel.
notes: Lead-in card before V35 ເ◌ົາ, the first vowel written before its consonant (owner 2026-11-13: teach the principle first, the vowel card keeps a short reminder). Standard Lao spelling fact (preposed vowels are pronounced after the initial consonant). No respellings (LESSON_RULES 13). Wording by agent. Owner 2026-11-13: card text trimmed (one point per sentence; one-unit principle on R03 only).

teach_en: Everyday Lao often leaves out 'I', 'you' or 'he/she' when it is clear who is meant. Asked ເຈົ້າຫິວນ້ຳບໍ່? ('Are you thirsty?'), you can answer ຫິວນ້ຳ ('I'm thirsty') with no 'I'. This is normal everyday Lao.
notes: PLAN L1d (b), owner play-test 2026-11-13. Placed after S000002889 ຫິວນ້ຳ (reply to S000001170 ເຈົ້າຫິວນ້ຳບໍ່?) rather than at ບໍ່ຫິວ: the native speaker endorsed ຫິວເຂົ້າ / ຫິວນ້ຳ, while bare ບໍ່ຫິວ as a reply is still asked in QUESTIONS (curriculum review). ຂ້ອຍ is taught only in L0010, so pronouns are named in English. No respellings in the text (LESSON_RULES 13). Wording by agent.
